documentation.content: The uptime check calls /livez (process liveness only, no database access, so Neon can scale to zero). It does not cover the database or scheduler: open /health and inspect the database and scheduler heartbeats; HTTP 200 alone is insufficient. Check Cloud Run logs and docs/operations/operational-verification-2026-09-09.md. Do not weaken the trusted-edge or tenant controls.

conditions.displayName: Dependency health fails from two or more checkers

documentation.content: At least five HTTP 5xx responses in a five-minute aligned window. Inspect the active revision, failed endpoint classes, database and scheduled-job status. Avoid copying raw request/portfolio data into incident records.

conditionThreshold.filter: resource.type="cloud_run_revision" AND resource.labels.service_name="portfyl" AND metric.type="run.googleapis.com/request_count" AND metric.labels.response_code_class="5xx"

documentation.content: Cloud Scheduler reported an error for a Portfyl job. Check OIDC audience/caller, service configuration and job logs. Heartbeat-based detection also covers stale successful runs.

A user's Trading 212 history import stopped in needs_review: Trading 212 sent something Portfyl cannot import safely yet (unknown cash type, contradicting sign, unsupported corporate action, bad data). The `detail` label lists the stream, provider type, date, currency, sign and reason, never amounts. Teach the mapper in backend/t212_cash.py or t212_corporate_actions.py, deploy, then ask the user to press Retry history import. Find the full line in Cloud Run logs by searching for the run id.
